## Decision questions

1. Canonical version and exact supported legacy versions.
2. STDIO compatibility probe behavior when server/discover is unknown to an older client.
3. Whether protocol support remains hand-rolled, adopts an official SDK, or isolates schema-derived wire contracts behind the public pm SDK.
4. Streamable HTTP deployment and authorization scope.
5. Removal or adapter policy for initialize, notifications/initialized, ping, logging/setLevel, roots changes, resource subscriptions, SSE resumability, and deprecated features.
6. Capability and extension negotiation when a caller omits or conflicts with request metadata.
7. Rollout, metrics, sunset criteria, and rollback without mutable history.

## Preferred direction

Use the official schema as the normative wire contract, keep transport-neutral semantics in the public pm SDK, make 2026-07-28 the default, and retain only explicitly tested compatibility adapters that do not recreate protocol-level sessions.
ADR: MCP 2026-07-28 is canonical and legacy interoperability is a bounded stateless adapter, not connection-local session state
Choose the protocol-version, transport, compatibility, and dependency strategy for replacing the 2025-06-18 initialize handshake without preserving forbidden session semantics.

The accepted decision names canonical and supported legacy protocol versions plus a sunset policy; The decision resolves hand-rolled versus official-SDK usage while preserving the public pm SDK as the policy boundary; STDIO and Streamable HTTP negotiation, discovery, compatibility probes, and unsupported-version errors are specified; Every removed or deprecated feature has an explicit remove, adapt, or migrate disposition with security rationale; Rollout telemetry, negative controls, rollback, and released-artifact gates are defined before implementation starts
Interoperable current MCP without ambiguous dual semantics
Approve one explicit compatibility policy for 2026-07-28 core behavior, legacy clients, transports, extensions, and deprecations
Implementation teams can migrate once against a stable architecture and test matrix
Every downstream protocol child depends on whether initialize, ping, sessions, server-initiated requests, and legacy HTTP behavior remain adapters or are removed
